--- title: "sportsdataverse-py" subtitle: "Tidy, cross-sport play-by-play, box score, schedule, roster & betting data for Python" toc: false about: template: jolla image: "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-py/master/sdv-py-logo.png" links: - icon: github text: GitHub href: https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-py - icon: box text: PyPI href: https://pypi.org/project/sportsdataverse/ - icon: book text: Docusaurus docs href: https://py.sportsdataverse.org --- `sportsdataverse-py` is the Python sister to the SportsDataverse R packages (`hoopR`, `wehoop`, `cfbfastR`, `baseballr`, `fastRhockey`) and gives you tidy [polars](https://pola.rs) / [pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org) access to play-by-play, box score, schedule, roster, and odds data across the NBA, WNBA, NFL, MLB, NHL, men's & women's college basketball, college football, soccer, cricket, junior hockey, and more. ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} This site is a **Quarto + Great-Docs conversion** of the production [Docusaurus docs](https://py.sportsdataverse.org), built to evaluate Quarto's literate, *run-it-for-real* documentation model against the current React/MDX stack. Every table and number below is the **genuine output of `sportsdataverse` code executed at build time** and frozen into the static page — no client-side Python, no hand-maintained "expected output" that can drift. See the [evaluation write-up](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-py/blob/proto/quarto-docs/docs-quarto/README.md). ::: ## Install ::: {.panel-tabset} ### pip ```bash pip install sportsdataverse ``` ### uv ```bash uv add sportsdataverse ``` ### conda ```bash conda install -c conda-forge sportsdataverse ``` ::: Requires Python 3.9–3.14. The DataFrame engine is polars 1.x; every loader can hand back pandas with `return_as_pandas=True`. ## The surface, in one cell First, import the package and confirm the per-sport namespaces resolve. This is a stable, offline-safe call — it touches no network. ::: {#3f0303b8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") # silence the harmless numexpr/bottleneck UserWarning import sportsdataverse as sdv sports = ["nba", "wnba", "nfl", "mlb", "nhl", "mbb", "wbb", "cfb", "odds"] present = [s for s in sports if hasattr(sdv, s)] present ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['nba', 'wnba', 'nfl', 'mlb', 'nhl', 'mbb', 'wbb', 'cfb', 'odds'] ``` ::: ::: Each sport submodule exposes an `espn__*` family of tidy-data loaders. For example, the NBA namespace ships a large ESPN endpoint surface: ::: {#19d6ce2a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import sportsdataverse.nba as nba nba_espn = [fn for fn in dir(nba) if fn.startswith("espn_nba_")] print(f"{len(nba_espn)} espn_nba_* callables; first 12:") nba_espn[:12] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 115 espn_nba_* callables; first 12: ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['espn_nba_award', 'espn_nba_awards', 'espn_nba_calendar', 'espn_nba_coach', 'espn_nba_coach_record', 'espn_nba_coach_season', 'espn_nba_conferences', 'espn_nba_draft', 'espn_nba_franchise', 'espn_nba_franchises', 'espn_nba_game', 'espn_nba_game_broadcasts'] ``` ::: ::: ## A real loader → a real DataFrame Call `espn_nba_teams()` — a stable ESPN teams endpoint — and let Quarto render the returned **polars** DataFrame as an HTML table. This is *live data captured at build time*, not a sample that drifts out of date. ::: {#31f2504f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_teams teams = espn_nba_teams() # -> polars.DataFrame teams.select(["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_display_name"]).head(10) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
shape: (10, 3)

"1""ATL""Atlanta Hawks"

"9""GS""Golden State Warriors"
``` ::: ::: The cross-league surface is uniform: `espn__teams()` returns the same tidy shape for every league. Here is the NFL equivalent: ::: {#d4276148 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sportsdataverse.nfl import espn_nfl_teams espn_nfl_teams().select(["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_display_name"]).head(8) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
shape: (8, 3)

``` ::: ::: ## Inline computed results in prose Quarto supports **inline executable expressions**, so a sentence can quote a *computed* number rather than a copy-pasted one that goes stale. ::: {#5342cf21 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} n_nba = espn_nba_teams().height n_nfl = espn_nfl_teams().height ``` ::: As of this render, `sportsdataverse` reports **30 NBA teams** and **32 NFL teams** from the ESPN teams endpoints — both computed by Python while this page was being built. ## Where to go next ::: {.grid} ::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4} ### [Guides »](guides/index.qmd) Executable walkthroughs: install, teams & scoreboard, schedule & rosters, and the polars/pandas parser layer. ::: ::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4} ### [Reference »](reference/index.qmd) Hand-written reference for MLB & NBA with real `df.head()` output, plus generator-emitted stubs proving the codegen → `.qmd` path. ::: ::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4} ### [Architecture »](architecture.qmd) The ESPN cross-league core, the parser layer, and the codegen pipeline that drives the production docs. ::: :::
